# Architecture catalog

Catalog date: 2026-11-16. For changing B2 product details, use <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning> as the authority.

## Collect and curate image-text corpora into streamable training shards

Bulk-download URL and caption lists into WebDataset shards on B2, score them for CLIP alignment, quality, NSFW and near-duplicates, and write filtered subsets as new immutable shards with a subset manifest. Raw shards are never rewritten; diffusion training streams the subsets directly.

**Use when:** Text-to-image corpora hold millions to billions of image-text pairs, and filtering strategy drives model quality. Teams must keep the raw pool and several filtered subsets reproducible without copying them to local disks or rewriting raw data.

**Workflow:** Write URL and caption lists to `raw/<corpus>/urls/` → Run img2dataset with webdataset output to an s3:// output_folder whose fsspec endpoint is the B2 S3 endpoint → Stream shards through CLIP scoring, Data-Juicer recipes, NSFW classifiers and fastdup; write scores to stats/ and embeddings to embeddings/ → Record excluded sample keys as parquet exclusion lists under `quarantine/<run>/` instead of rewriting raw shards → Re-pack kept samples into `filtered/<recipe-version>/` shards and write the subset manifest last → Stream filtered shards into PyTorch with WebDataset using per-worker and per-node shard splits

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Multipart upload for large tar shards, Object Lock on a dedicated raw-corpus bucket, Prefix lifecycle rules for scores and intermediates, Prefix-scoped application keys, Presigned URLs as an alternative shard transport.

**Integrations:** [img2dataset](https://github.com/rom1504/img2dataset) (fsspec / s3fs) — Set output_folder to `s3://<bucket>/<prefix>` and put client_kwargs.endpoint_url `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` in ~/.config/fsspec/s3.json; write webdataset or parquet output (the tfrecord writer bypasses fsspec); [s3fs (fsspec)](https://s3fs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) (fsspec / s3fs) — Pass endpoint_url `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` to S3FileSystem (or client_kwargs.endpoint_url in fsspec config) with a scoped B2 application key as key and secret; [WebDataset](https://github.com/webdataset/webdataset) (S3 custom endpoint) — Open shards with `pipe:aws s3 cp --endpoint-url https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com s3://<bucket>/<shard>.tar -`, a gopen handler backed by boto3 with endpoint_url, or presigned HTTPS shard URLs; [LanceDB](https://lancedb.com/) (S3 custom endpoint) — Use the pinned LanceDB 0.20.0 / pylance 0.23.2 connection profile in examples/lancedb.md, with the B2 endpoint, region and scoped credentials; serialize all table mutations through one writer service ([setup guide](https://github.com/lance-format/lance/blob/v0.23.2/rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs)).

**Keep off B2:** Job and shard queue (Ray or Redis); Crawl dedup and robots cache; Dataset catalog database with corpus records, licenses and recipe-to-subset mapping; Live vector index that serves similarity queries; GPU-local NVMe read-ahead cache.

**Scale:** Millions to billions of image-text pairs in shards of roughly 0.3-1 GB. Standard B2 is the default. Measure sustained multi-node shard-read throughput before considering Overdrive; add a node-local read-ahead cache for repeated epochs over the same subset.

**Security:** Give the downloader a write-only ingest key scoped to raw/ and training jobs a read-only key scoped to filtered/; Keep the curation key unable to delete from the raw-corpus bucket; Object Lock enforces it independently; Treat presigned shard URLs as bearer credentials with short TTLs.

## Fine-tune LoRA and diffusion models with versioned checkpoints

Train LoRA, DreamBooth or full fine-tunes on curated subsets, and write each run's dataset snapshot, captions, checkpoints, sample grids and final .safetensors to run-scoped prefixes so interrupted runs resume and released weights trace back to their data.

**Use when:** Checkpoints range from MB-scale LoRAs to tens of GB with optimizer state. Spot GPUs need resume-from-latest, and the most common trainers write only to local disk.

**Workflow:** Snapshot the training subset and captions to `runs/<run_id>/dataset/` and write run.json → Train with Ray Train using a B2 storage_path, or run diffusers or kohya scripts locally and sync output with rclone → Write intermediate state to `checkpoints/<run_id>/` and sample grids to `samples/<run_id>/`, and keep finals in `runs/<run_id>/final/` → Log params, metrics and the final LoRA to MLflow with a b2:// artifact URI and register the model version → Pin dataset and LoRA versions to git with DVC → For hosted training, pass Replicate a presigned GET URL to the dataset zip and copy the resulting weights back to B2 → Expire intermediates by lifecycle rule and publish released weights to a separate Object Lock bucket

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Multipart upload for multi-GB checkpoints, Prefix lifecycle rules for intermediate checkpoints, Object Lock on a dedicated released-weights bucket, Prefix-scoped application keys per run or tenant, Presigned URLs for hosted-training handoff.

**Integrations:** [Ray Train](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/user-guides/persistent-storage.html) (S3 custom endpoint) — Set RunConfig storage_path to `s3://<bucket>/checkpoints?endpoint_override=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, or set AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 with AWS credential variables holding a B2 application key; Ray's persistent-storage guide covers Backblaze B2; [MLflow](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/) (Built-in Backblaze B2 option) — Artifact store URI `b2://<bucket>@s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<path>` with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION set to a B2 application key and region; [DVC](https://doc.dvc.org/user-guide/data-management/remote-storage/amazon-s3) (S3 custom endpoint) — Run `dvc remote modify <remote> endpointurl https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` and store the B2 application key with `dvc remote modify --local` access_key_id and secret_access_key; [rclone](https://rclone.org/b2/) (Built-in Backblaze B2 option) — Use the native `b2` backend with a scoped application key (or the `s3` backend with the B2 endpoint); `rclone sync` and `rclone copy` move data between B2 and local disk; [Replicate](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/input-files) (Presigned URLs) — Presigned B2 GET URLs passed as hosted-file inputs; outputs are copied back to B2 because API output files are deleted after one hour ([setup guide](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/data-retention)).

**Keep off B2:** GPU-local NVMe scratch for active shards and in-progress checkpoint writes; MLflow backend store (Postgres or MySQL) with metrics, stages and aliases; Job scheduler state; Replicate's transient training storage.

**Scale:** Tens to thousands of runs, with checkpoints from MB-scale LoRAs to tens of GB with optimizer state. Standard B2 handles checkpoint writes and resume reads. Lifecycle rules on checkpoints/ keep storage from growing with every step.

**Security:** Scope trainer keys to one run or tenant prefix; trainers never hold delete rights on the released-weights bucket; Issue presigned dataset URLs to hosted trainers with the shortest TTL that covers the job start; Keep MLflow and DVC credentials in environment or secret stores, never in tracked config.

## Distribute base checkpoints and LoRAs to a GPU inference fleet

Keep base checkpoints, VAEs, ControlNets and LoRAs once under a B2 models/ prefix; ComfyUI hosts, serverless GPU functions and CI pull from it into node-local caches with read-only keys and skip unchanged files.

**Use when:** SDXL and FLUX weights are several GB each and catalogs hold hundreds to thousands of LoRAs. Re-downloading from public hubs on every new GPU node is slow and rate-limited, and copies drift across the fleet.

**Workflow:** CI publishes approved weights under immutable versioned keys in models/, with model card and license beside them, and writes a mutable latest pointer last → Mirror Hugging Face hub caches to B2 under team prefixes with hf-cache-sync → ComfyUI hosts pull into models/ with the Download Model from Cloud node, which skips files whose ETag matches → Modal functions mount the models/ prefix read-only with CloudBucketMount and a B2 bucket_endpoint_url → Bulk-migrate existing checkpoint libraries and pre-warm nodes with rclone → Prune node-local caches with LRU eviction; B2 stays the source of truth

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, ETag comparison for change detection, Multipart upload, Read-only prefix-scoped application keys, Object Lock or versioning on released weights, Cloud Replication for multi-region fleets.

**Integrations:** [ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/comfyui-cloud-storage) (Built-in Backblaze B2 option) — "Backblaze B2" provider preset (COMFY_S3_PROVIDER, COMFY_S3_REGION) or COMFY_S3_ENDPOINT_URL; credentials resolve from env vars or a server-side JSON profile, never workflow JSON; [hf-cache-sync](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/hf-cache-sync) (Built-in Backblaze B2 option) — Set B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID, B2_APPLICATION_KEY, B2_BUCKET, B2_REGION and B2_ENDPOINT (or the YAML storage block); the boto3 client talks to the B2 S3 endpoint; [Modal CloudBucketMount](https://modal.com/docs/reference/modal.CloudBucketMount) (S3 custom endpoint) — `CloudBucketMount(bucket_name, bucket_endpoint_url="https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com", key_prefix="models/", read_only=True, secret=...)` with a secret holding a B2 application key; [rclone](https://rclone.org/b2/) (Built-in Backblaze B2 option) — Use the native `b2` backend with a scoped application key (or the `s3` backend with the B2 endpoint); `rclone sync` and `rclone copy` move data between B2 and local disk.

**Keep off B2:** Node-local model directories and caches that the runtime loads from; Model registry metadata (stages, aliases, approvals); ComfyUI workflow JSON, which must hold no credentials; Inference GPU memory.

**Scale:** Hundreds to thousands of weight files from MB-scale LoRAs to tens of GB, pulled by tens to thousands of GPU nodes. Standard B2 for publish and steady-state pulls. Fleet-wide cold starts that pull the same large files at once are the case to measure for Overdrive; node-local caches remove repeat reads.

**Security:** Only CI holds write keys to models/; workers get listFiles and readFiles on the models/ prefix; Verify SHA-256 from the model card or manifest after download; multipart ETags are not content hashes; Keep provider credentials out of shareable ComfyUI workflow JSON.

## Generate images and persist every output with provenance manifests

Text-to-image and edit apps call self-hosted pipelines or hosted APIs, write every output to B2 immediately, and store a SHA-256 manifest of provider, model, prompt, params, seed and parent asset beside it so remix lineage, replays and audits stay possible.

**Use when:** Hosted output URLs are ephemeral, and consumer apps produce millions of images a month. Without a durable store and manifests next to the bytes, lineage and replay are lost.

**Workflow:** The app or node graph submits a prompt; reference inputs go to the provider as presigned GET URLs → Application workers persist outputs and manifest.json under `runs/<tenant>/<date>/<run_id>/` or content-addressed `assets/<sha256>` → A separate audit publisher copies approved manifests to the audit bucket when retention is required → ComfyUI Save to Cloud nodes write graph outputs and return presigned share URLs → fal.ai and Replicate outputs are copied to B2 as soon as they arrive → Optionally sign C2PA in the app and store the sidecar next to the asset → Index outputs in the app database or Pixeltable tables; the bucket stays the system of record

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Presigned URLs for input handoff and private sharing, Per-tenant prefix-scoped application keys, Prefix lifecycle rules for abandoned drafts, Object Lock on a dedicated audit-manifest bucket, Event Notifications to trigger indexing.

**Integrations:** [ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/comfyui-cloud-storage) (Built-in Backblaze B2 option) — Save to Cloud and Load from Cloud nodes with the "Backblaze B2" provider preset; Generate Sharing URL node for presigned links; [fal.ai](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/fal-cdn) (Presigned URLs) — image_url inputs accept presigned S3-compatible URLs; outputs are copied back to B2; [Replicate](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/input-files) (Presigned URLs) — Presigned B2 GET URLs passed as hosted-file inputs; outputs are copied back to B2 because API output files are deleted after one hour ([setup guide](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/data-retention)); [Pixeltable](https://docs.pixeltable.com/integrations/cloud-storage) (Built-in Backblaze B2 option) — Backblaze B2 destination `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<bucket>/<prefix>/` with b2_profile in config.toml and keys under a [b2] AWS credentials profile.

**Keep off B2:** Request queue and GPU worker state; Rate limits, credits and billing; User, gallery and prompt-history database; Prompt and result caches; C2PA signing keys.

**Scale:** Thousands to millions of generated images per month, each a few hundred KB to a few MB, plus a small manifest. Request count, not bandwidth, dominates. Standard B2 fits; batch small writes where the SDK allows and keep listing out of hot request paths.

**Security:** Use per-tenant prefix-scoped keys or a server-side signer that enforces the tenant prefix; Give providers presigned GETs with short TTLs, never application keys; Keep C2PA signing keys in a KMS or HSM, not in the bucket.

## Ingest, moderate and purge user-uploaded reference images

Browsers upload selfies, product photos and reference images directly to a private uploads/ prefix with presigned PUTs; an Event Notification triggers moderation and EXIF stripping; approved items reach edit APIs and likeness-LoRA training only as short-lived presigned GETs, and subject deletion coordinates active writers, every B2 version, quarantined originals, and provider copies.

**Use when:** Uploads are PII- and biometric-adjacent, arrive at high request counts, and must not flow through app servers. Teams need moderation before use, short retention and verifiable deletion.

**Workflow:** The app issues a presigned PUT, through Uppy Companion or its own API, scoped to `uploads/<tenant>/<subject>/`; CORS allows only the app origin → A B2 Event Notification on object creation triggers moderation → Approved items are EXIF-stripped and the stripped bytes are PUT to `approved/<tenant>/<subject>/`; rejected items are copied server-side to `quarantine/<tenant>/<subject>/<batch>/`; decisions go to `audit/moderation/<tenant>/<subject>/` → Approved references go to fal.ai or Replicate edit and LoRA-training endpoints as short-expiry presigned GET URLs → Outputs return to `subjects/<tenant>/<subject>/outputs/`; the consent DB inventories B2 versions and provider request/model IDs → A deletion request marks the subject deleting, blocks new signing and writes, drains active uploads/jobs, and confirms provider deletion or data-retention expiry before completing

**B2 capabilities:** Presigned PUT and GET URLs, CORS rules for browser uploads, Event Notifications with signed webhooks, Server-side copy for quarantine routing, Prefix lifecycle rules for raw-upload expiry, Prefix-scoped application keys, SSE-B2 encryption at rest.

**Integrations:** [Uppy + Companion](https://uppy.io/docs/companion/) (S3 custom endpoint) — Set s3.endpoint (COMPANION_AWS_ENDPOINT) to `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` and s3.region to the bucket region; browsers upload straight to the bucket with presigned PUT or multipart requests, so configure bucket CORS; [fal.ai](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/fal-cdn) (Presigned URLs) — Short-expiry presigned GETs of approved references passed as image_url inputs; [Replicate](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/input-files) (Presigned URLs) — Presigned GET of the approved image set as the hosted-file input for LoRA training ([setup guide](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/data-retention)).

**Keep off B2:** Auth and user database; Consent and retention records; Moderation decision and appeal database; Processing queue; Classifier GPU or CPU workers.

**Scale:** Many small uploads (a few to dozens per subject) with bursty request rates. Request count and event throughput dominate, not bandwidth. Keep the webhook fast and idempotent and do the heavy work from a queue.

**Security:** Never expose application keys to browsers; sign uploads server-side for an exact key and content type; Verify X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature and process events idempotently; Do not enable Object Lock on the uploads bucket, or per-subject purge cannot complete; Strip EXIF (including GPS) before any third-party handoff.

## Serve generated galleries through a CDN with on-the-fly variants

Approved outputs are served from a private B2 origin through Cloudflare Workers or a bunny.net pull zone with S3 authentication, and imgproxy resizes and converts originals on request so per-size variants live in the edge cache instead of the bucket.

**Use when:** Galleries get far more reads than writes, with long-tail access to old generations. Storing every thumbnail size multiplies object counts, and serving directly from the origin raises egress costs.

**Workflow:** Promote approved outputs to a delivery prefix and set Cache-Control at upload → A Cloudflare Worker signs origin requests to the private bucket with a read-only key, or a bunny.net pull zone uses S3 authentication → imgproxy reads originals from B2 and serves thumbnails and WebP or AVIF variants behind the CDN → Private items use short-lived presigned URLs instead of CDN paths → An Event Notification handler purges the CDN cache when an item is unpublished

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Read-only application keys for origin signing, Cache-Control set at upload, Presigned URLs for private items, Free egress to CDN partners.

**Integrations:** [Cloudflare Workers (private bucket)](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-deliver-private-backblaze-b2-content-through-cloudflare-cdn) (CDN origin) — Deploy a Worker that signs origin requests to `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` with a read-only application key; the bucket stays private behind the CDN; [bunny.net](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-bunnynet-with-backblaze-b2) (CDN origin) — Set the pull zone origin to the bucket's S3 URL, enable S3 Authentication with the key ID, application key and bucket region, and enable Block Root Path Access ([setup guide](https://docs.bunny.net/cdn/integrations/storage/backblaze)); [imgproxy](https://docs.imgproxy.net/image_sources/amazon_s3) (S3 custom endpoint) — Set `IMGPROXY_USE_S3=true`, `IMGPROXY_S3_ENDPOINT=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` and `IMGPROXY_S3_REGION` to the bucket region; source URLs use `s3://<bucket>/<key>`.

**Keep off B2:** CDN edge cache; imgproxy cache; Gallery and feed database and search index; Like and view counters; Worker secrets store.

**Scale:** Read-heavy galleries with long-tail access across millions of images. CDN cache hit rate decides origin load. Store originals once and let the edge cache variants; Overdrive is not usually the bottleneck here.

**Security:** Keep the bucket private and give the CDN a read-only key scoped to the delivery prefix; Sign imgproxy URLs so the transformer cannot be used as an open proxy; Never route private items through shared CDN caches; use presigned URLs instead.

## Related sample applications

Sample applications for these storage workflows. Each linked repository includes source code and setup instructions.

- [img2dataset to WebDataset on B2](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/img2dataset-webdataset-object-storage): img2dataset shards, parquet and stats streamed into B2 with no local staging.
- [DataComp image-text filtering](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/datacomp-image-text-filtering): CLIP scoring of streamed shards with filtered shards and metrics written back.
- [Data-Juicer multimodal curation](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/data-juicer-multimodal-curation): Data-Juicer recipes over raw shards with refined outputs and stats per run.
- [fastdup dataset cleaning](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/fastdup-dataset-cleaning): Duplicate, outlier and broken-file detection with server-side-copy quarantine.
- [OpenCLIP batch embeddings](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/openclip-batch-embeddings): OpenCLIP .npy embedding shards and a FAISS index per job on B2.
- [WebDataset streaming PyTorch training](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/webdataset-streaming-pytorch-training): Tar shards streamed from B2 through a boto3-backed s3:// opener.
- [Lance multimodal search](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lance-multimodal-search): LanceDB multimodal tables on B2 for image similarity search.
- [LoRA Training Studio](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lora-training-studio): Diffusers and peft LoRA training with every artifact under a run prefix.
- [AI Headshot Studio](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/ai-headshot-studio): Likeness LoRA from selfies with presigned-only access and per-subject purge.
- [hf-cache-sync](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/hf-cache-sync): Hugging Face hub cache shared across machines through B2 with LRU pruning.
- [Backblaze B2 GitHub Action](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/b2-action): CI upload, sync, verify, presign and Object Lock retention verbs.
- [ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/comfyui-cloud-storage): ComfyUI save, load, model-cache and presigned-share nodes.
- [Genblaze SDK](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze): Provider-agnostic generation with SHA-256 provenance manifests on B2.
- [Genblaze multi-provider sample](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze-gen-media-multi-provider-sample): Multi-provider pipeline with run-scoped prefixes and lifecycle suggestions.
- [Genblaze x GMICloud pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze-gmicloud-pipeline): Anchor image fanned out to video models with manifests on B2.
